user_input: I cleared my DSA coding rounds, got an 8.9 CGPA this sem, and my dad is already brag-calling relatives about my upcoming Amazon internship. But I just sat on my bed tonight looking at the wall for three hours. It all feels so empty. Why am I killing myself coding until 3 AM just to sit in a cubicle and make some rich guy richer? None of this actually matters, does it?

Everyone on LinkedIn is posting these obnoxious 'pleased to share' updates about their placements at top-tier firms. I scroll through them and feel this cold, dead sensation in my chest. Even if I get those 20 LPA packages, then what? Is life just a series of upgrading your phone, paying EMIs, and waiting to die? I feel completely disconnected from everything.

I failed my system design midterms, and my CGPA dropped to 6.8. My roommates are discussing system architecture in the mess, and I just stared at my plate of cold rice. If I can't even clear these basic engineering papers, what am I even doing here? It feels like I'm playing a game where the rules were written for someone else, and my presence here doesn't change a single thing in this universe.

I'm turning twenty next week, and the sheer routine of my life is suffocating. I wake up, attend lectures I don't care about, debug some stupid code, sleep, and repeat. My parents keep asking about my 'career roadmap' but I don't even have a roadmap for tomorrow. I feel like a ghost drifting through a campus that doesn't care if I exist or not.

I changed my major to Humanities because I hated Tech, but now I'm sitting in these lectures on existentialism and it's making everything worse. I look at my peers who are struggling to pay rent or get low-paying internships, and I look at myself, and I'm just tired. What was the point of pivoting if the destination is just another flavor of survival and disappointment?

I just cleared my DSA coding lab test and got a 9.5 CGPA this semester, but I sat on my bed looking at the screen and felt absolutely nothing. Like, why am I grinding 14 hours a day to solve LeetCode problems just to join a company and make some rich guy richer while my youth just slips away? My dad keeps telling me about my cousin's 30 LPA package, but honestly, even if I get that, it feels completely hollow and pointless.

I'm in my final year and everyone is frantically updating their LinkedIn, posting about their summer internships, and pretending they love this corporate hustle. I spent three hours last night looking at the ceiling, wondering if this is all life is—getting a degree, working a 9-to-5, paying bills, and dying. If there's no actual point to any of this, how am I supposed to find the energy to wake up for my 8 AM lectures tomorrow?

I had this big dream of getting into CS, but now that I'm actually here writing compilers and operating system labs, I feel so disconnected. We're just memorizing syntax and running test cases, and it feels like none of this actually matters to the world or to me. I look at my classmates who are so driven, and I just feel like an absolute ghost sitting in the back of the lecture hall, wondering why I even exist.

My parents keep talking about my future security and how this upcoming placement drive will define the rest of my life. But I feel this crushing apathy; I don't care about the placement, I don't care about the salary, and I don't even care if I fail. When everything feels so completely transient and minor in the grand scheme of things, how do people find the motivation to care about mock interviews and aptitude tests?

I finished my midterms and actually did pretty well, but instead of feeling happy, I just felt this deep, heavy silence in my chest. It's like I'm running on a treadmill that's going faster and faster, but there's no destination—just more exams, more projects, and more endless expectations. I'm so tired of pretending that getting an A is some life-altering victory when it actually changes absolutely nothing about how empty I feel inside.

Just finished a 14-hour grind for the upcoming DSA lab exam and looked at my git commits. I got the code to compile, but I just stared at the terminal and felt this bizarre, hollow emptiness. What am I even doing? If I clear this, it's just placements, then a 9-to-5 corporate slog, then what? Why does everyone act like getting a 15 LPA package is the absolute peak of human existence when it feels so utterly pointless?

My CGPA came out today and I actually managed an 8.9. My mom was literally crying tears of joy on the phone, telling our relatives how hard I worked. But inside, I felt absolutely nothing. It’s like I’m wearing a mask of this high-achieving student while my actual self is just drowning in a vacuum where nothing matters. What's the point of running a race where even winning feels like losing?

Scrolling through LinkedIn is giving me literal vertigo. Everyone is posting about their summer internships at FAANG, and my dad keeps asking when I'm going to start prepping for system design. I don't want to design scalable databases. I don't want to optimize code. I look at these tech stacks and I just see a massive, meaningless void of corporate jargon that has zero relevance to actual life.

I skipped my midterms today. Just stayed in bed staring at the ceiling fan spin. My roommate thinks I'm sick, but the truth is, I just couldn't find a single logical reason to get up and write answers about microprocessor architecture. It feels like we are all just pretending this matters so we don't have to face the terrifying fact that we are completely insignificant.

I'm in my final semester and everyone is talking about 'settling down' and building a career pathway. I look at my degree certificate and it just feels like a piece of paper that I wasted four years of my life to get. I didn't learn anything about how to live, how to cope with grief, or how to find joy—just how to pass exams. I feel completely unprepared for adulthood because the foundation feels totally empty.

I finally got the 18 LPA offer today. Everyone is congratulating me, my dad is bragging on WhatsApp, but I just sat in the bathroom and cried. I spent four years grinding DSA, sacrificing sleep, crying over pointers, and now that it's here... it feels like nothing. If this big 'achievement' is this hollow, what the hell am I even running for?

My CGPA is 9.4, but I swear I couldn't tell you one single thing I actually care about. I just wake up, memorize code snippets, vomit them on a paper, get the A, and repeat. I look at my classmates laughing or talking about their hobbies and I feel like an absolute ghost watching real humans live their lives. Is this it? Is this what the next forty years of IT corporate life is going to be?

I spent the whole night scrolling LinkedIn and seeing all these 'humbled and honored' posts from my batchmates landing remote internships. I went to the terrace at 3 AM and just stared at the sky, feeling so incredibly small. What is the point of all this competition? Even if I get an internship, then what? Another promotion? Another tech stack? It feels like we are just hamsters spinning a wheel that doesn't actually go anywhere.

I took Computer Science because everyone said it's the safest route to a good life, but I hate every second of it. I sit in my compiler design lecture and literally feel my chest tightening up with this heavy, cold dread. I feel like I've signed a contract to sell my youth for a paycheck, and now I'm trapped in a tunnel with no other exits. Why does everyone else seem so okay with this mindless compromise?

The semester exams ended two days ago and now the campus is totally quiet. I thought I'd be happy, but instead this massive wave of nothingness has just crushed me. When I'm busy studying, I can pretend I have a purpose, but now that the noise has stopped, I'm just sitting in my hostel room realizing I have absolutely no idea who I am or what I actually want from this life.

Just got my day-1 placement offer from a tier-1 firm, and everyone is celebrating, but I just came back to my hostel room and stared at the ceiling for two hours. I scraped through 8 semesters, spent nights grinding LeetCode and mugging up DBMS definitions, and for what? I don't feel happy, I just feel nothing... like I solved a puzzle I didn't care about, and now the prize is to do this for the next forty years.

I'm looking at my schedule for the next three weeks—midterms, OS labs, back-to-back coding contests, and a backlog exam to clear. It’s just this endless, repetitive loop of running to stand still, and I can't help but ask myself what the point of any of this is. Even if I get a 9 CGPA, we are all just meat in a grinder, waiting to get packaged and sold to some corporate giant that doesn't care if we exist.

Every time I open LinkedIn, I see classmates posting about their summer internships at high-frequency trading firms or getting research fellowships abroad. I look at my own resume, then at my ceiling, and I feel this deep, heavy pointlessness wash over me. Why are we competing so violently for things that don't actually matter to us, just to look good on a digital dashboard while feeling completely dead inside?

My dad spent the whole dinner talking about my cousin who got a 40 LPA package at a fintech startup, asking me what my 'game plan' is. I just sat there chewing my food, feeling this suffocating wave of numbness because I don't care about the 40 LPA, but I also don't know what I actually care about. It feels like I'm a blank space where a person is supposed to be, and I'm just playing along so my parents don't realize I'm completely empty inside.

I turned twenty-one last week, and instead of feeling excited, I just feel this crushing sense of dread. Graduation is next semester, and everyone is talking about moving to Bangalore or Hyderabad, renting flats, and starting their corporate lives. I look at this path of 'growing up' and it looks so incredibly bleak—wake up, code, meetings, sleep, repeat—is this really all there is to life?

I cleared the Amazon OA and got a 9.4 CGPA this semester, but honestly, I just sat on my balcony at 3 AM looking at the streetlights and felt absolutely nothing. Like, what is even the point of grinding 14 hours a day of LeetCode just to secure a package, buy a car, and die? Everyone is celebrating my shortlist but I feel this terrifying, hollow emptiness inside me that won't go away.

I’m in my final year and everyone is frantically updating their LinkedIn, talking about 'CTC' and 'tech stacks' like it's the only thing that matters in the universe. I look at these DSA sheets and system design videos and I just freeze up. It's not that I can't do it, it's that I don't care anymore, but if I say that out loud, my parents will think I'm a failure. I feel like an actor playing a role in a movie I absolutely hate.

We had this huge placement drive today and the guys who got placed were crying with joy, but all I could think was: 'And then what?' You work for thirty years, pay taxes, and grow old. I sat through three hours of SQL lectures today and felt this crushing weight of pointlessness, like I'm just a tiny cog in some giant, stupid machine that doesn't care if I live or die.

My dad kept bragging to our relatives during dinner about how my branch has 100% placements and how I'll be earning six figures soon. I literally had to go to the bathroom and throw up because of how nauseous the whole conversation made me. I have zero interest in this field, I don't care about the packages, but I'm too deep into my third year to pull out now. I feel completely trapped in a life that doesn't belong to me.

I’m paying lakhs in tuition fees just to secure a desk where I'll do the same repetitive tasks until I die. Everyone tells me to 'trust the process' but the process looks like a slow death, and I can't find a single reason to wake up for my 8 AM lab tomorrow.

I'm sitting in the library during the mid-semester break, surrounded by stacks of books on compiler design, and I just started crying silently. It’s not even that the syllabus is hard, it’s that it feels completely meaningless in the grand scheme of things. We are sitting on a spinning rock in the middle of nowhere, and my entire worth is being boiled down to a SGPA decimal point on a piece of paper. I feel so utterly insignificant and disconnected from everything.

I cleared the Amazon OA and got an 8.9 CGPA this semester, but honestly, I just sat at my desk last night looking at the DSA sheets and felt absolutely nothing. Like, why am I grinding Leetcode every single night just to write code for some corporate machine that doesn't care if I exist? Everyone's congratulating me, but I feel like a ghost walking through campus; it all feels so pointless and empty.

I look at my parents planning my whole life around 'the package' and comparing me to my cousin who got 24 LPA, and I just feel this deep, heavy hollow space in my chest. What is the actual point of this whole race? Even if I get that salary, we're all just going to die anyway, and none of these stupid Excel sheets or system design interviews will have mattered. I'm just so tired of pretending that this matters to me.

Just registered for the upcoming placement drive and looking at the company list made me want to throw up. It's not even fear of rejection anymore, it's this weird panic that I'll actually get the job and then have to do this meaningless routine for forty years until I'm old. Is this really the grand prize of life—spending 10 hours a day debugging code so some VP can get a bigger bonus? I feel like I'm suffocating.

It's 3 AM during semester break and I'm staring at my ceiling wondering why I even exist. I cleared my backlogs, my CGPA is decent now, but I have zero desire to do anything tomorrow, or the day after that. I feel like an empty shell going through the motions of attending labs, eating, and sleeping just because it's what humans are supposed to do. I don't feel sad, just totally vacant and detached from my own life.

I spent the entire weekend scrolling LinkedIn seeing everyone post about their 'thrilled to announce' summer internships at top tech companies. I tried to feel happy for them, but instead, I just felt this deep, heavy wave of insignificance. It's like we're all playing this stupid game of pretending we care about 'innovative solutions' when we're just desperate for validation, and I'm so exhausted of pretending I want to play.

I just got my midterms back and I’m in the top 5% of my branch. Everyone is congratulating me, my dad is already talking about 30 LPA packages, but I went back to my hostel room, looked at my DSA LeetCode tracker, and just felt this cold, dead numbness. Why am I doing this? If the prize at the end of this four-year torture is just sitting in a cubicle writing API endpoints for some fintech company to make rich people richer, what is the actual point of being alive?

It's 3 AM and I'm looking at my resume draft for campus placements. Every project, every internship certificate feels like a lie I've crafted to please some HR manager. My friends are staying up drinking coffee, grinding system design questions, and I'm just sitting here staring at the ceiling fan spinning. We are all just copying and pasting our lives from some template, and it feels so incredibly meaningless. Is this all adult life is? A series of checkboxes until you die?

I attended three lectures today, submitted a compiler design lab, and ate cold mess food. I looked around the lecture hall and everyone looked like zombies, just copying slides down. I don't feel sad, I just feel totally empty, like a ghost walking through campus. If I disappeared tomorrow, the college database would just delete my roll number and nothing would change in the universe. How do people wake up every day and pretend any of this matters?

My mom called today crying because my cousin got a 45 LPA domestic offer at a top tech firm, and she asked me why I haven't updated my LinkedIn yet. I hung up and just sat on my bed for three hours. Everyone is chasing these titles and packages, but when I think about working 14 hours a day just to buy a bigger car or show off, it feels so deeply hollow. I feel like an alien because I don't want any of this, but I have no idea what else to do, so I just do nothing.

I turned twenty last week and it hit me like a train that the childhood magic is permanently gone. Now it’s just CGPA, backlogs, rent, tax calculations, and choosing a corporate sector to sell my soul to. I tried to study for my semester exams tonight but the formulas just looked like meaningless ink on paper. Why are we forced into this system where we trade our youth for survival, only to realize there was never any real goal at the end anyway?

I cleared the Amazon prelims today, and everyone is congratulating me in the batch group chat. But I just sat in the library looking at the screen feeling absolutely nothing. It's like I'm running this endless sprint for a package and a title, and even when I win a round, I just feel this cold, hollow space inside me. What is even the point of grinding 14 hours of DSA everyday if the prize at the end feels like empty air?

I look at my 9.2 CGPA and then I look out of my hostel window at 3 AM and just feel like a total ghost. My parents keep telling their friends how proud they are that I'll get a high package, but it feels like they are proud of a machine, not me. I don't even know what I like anymore; I've spent four years just optimizing for a resume, and now that the resume is perfect, I feel completely hollow and empty inside.

Everyone on LinkedIn is posting these flashy 'Happy to share' updates about their summer internships, and I'm sitting here with two backlogs wondering why I'm even alive. I tried opening my IDE to practice LeetCode, but I just stared at the cursor blinking for two hours. It felt like the blinking cursor was mocking me, asking me why I'm even trying when none of this actually matters in the grand scheme of things.

I went to the college fest today, surrounded by thousands of people screaming and dancing, and I've never felt more isolated in my entire life. I had to go to the washroom stall just to sit on the closed toilet seat and breathe in the dark. We are all pretending to have the best time of our lives, but it all feels like this massive, desperate performance to ignore how completely directionless and empty we all are.

I'm in my final semester, only a few weeks away from graduation, and everyone is talking about moving to Bangalore or Hyderabad and setting up their flats. But when I look at that future—renting a 1BHK, sitting in traffic, coding for some fintech giant—my chest just tightens up. It feels like I'm about to step off a cliff into a lifetime of grey, mundane routine that means absolutely nothing to me.

I cracked a 9.4 CGPA this semester, finished my DSA sheet, and my parents are already bragging about my upcoming placements to the relatives. But honestly? I sat on my terrace tonight and felt absolutely nothing. Just this hollow, empty pit. I’ve done everything I was supposed to do, but it feels like I'm just climbing a ladder that leans against a blank wall. What is even the point of all this grind if the prize at the end feels just as empty?

Every single day I open LinkedIn and see people from my batch posting about their 40 LPA packages and Google internships. I tried coding today but stared at the screen for three hours without writing a line of Python. It's like my brain has gone completely offline because it realized how utterly meaningless my little efforts are in this massive ocean. Even if I get that job, I'll just be another corporate cog spending 10 hours a day debugging code for someone else's profit—why do we pretend this is living?

I wake up at 7 AM, rush to attendance-mandatory lectures, write lab records I don't care about, go back to my hostel, eat cold mess food, and sleep. I looked at my schedule for the next two years and literally started crying because it's just this identical loop over and over. I feel like a ghost inhabiting a student's body, just watching myself go through the motions without any real spark or purpose. Is this all adult life is going to be—just a series of boxes to check until we die?

I turned twenty last week and it hit me like a train. I've spent my entire youth studying for board exams, JEE, and now college GPA, and for what? I don't even know what I actually like or who I am when I'm not studying. I feel like I've traded my real, actual life for a piece of paper and a career path I don't even care about, and now I'm too deep into this engineering branch to change anything.

Everyone around me is preparing for placement season like it's a war they've been training for their whole lives, discussing packages, mock interviews, and resume building in the mess. I listen to them and I feel completely detached, like I'm speaking a different language. I don't want to compete, I don't want to climb the ladder, but I also don't know what else to do, so I just sit in my room staring at the ceiling feeling this immense, crushing weight of uselessness.
